evidence: Enum types are used consistently and correctly throughout: GoalStatus, ProviderType, ConnectionState, ServerStatus, RecipeSource, SidebarPosition all appear in domain comparisons rather than raw string/int literals
ProviderType::parse() returns Option<ProviderType> and is called with .and_then() — correct use of the type system at the string-to-enum boundary

InstalledRecipe::installed_at (registry.rs:20) and Goal::created_at/updated_at (goals/types.rs:53-55) are typed as String but carry ISO-8601 semantic contracts — weaker than using chrono::DateTime<Utc>
GoalTree::storage_path uses .expect("home directory must exist") in production code (goals/tree.rs:73) — panics instead of returning Result, breaking the error contract implied by the caller path

Multiple #[allow(dead_code)] suppressions on public API structs/fns in tutorial/tracer.rs, tutorial/explain/constructs.rs, tutorial/explain/commands.rs without explanation — suppresses legitimate type visibility signals

McpToolInfo (colony-recipe/mcp_lifecycle.rs:33-37) and ToolInfo (colony-mcp/connection.rs:56-61) are parallel type definitions for the same concept with slightly different shapes; callers must manually map between them
SidebarConfig::panels and collapsed_panels are Vec<String> panel ID lists (ui-core/sidebar/manager.rs:15-16); a newtype PanelId or enum would prevent mixing with arbitrary strings
Public API functions across seed files are generally well-annotated with specific types; no dict[str, Any] equivalent or untyped public parameters observed
No type: ignore equivalent comments found in production code paths of the seed files
type_safety.issues_preventing_higher_score: Timestamp fields typed as String across multiple structs (registry, goals) represent a systematic weak-typing pattern. The GoalTree::storage_path panic in production code violates the error contract. Parallel ToolInfo definitions across crates require manual mapping and risk shape divergence.

strengths: Enum-first design is consistent: GoalStatus, ProviderType, ConnectionState, ServerStatus, RecipeSource, and SidebarPosition are all used at comparison sites rather than bypassed with raw strings or integers
Option/Result types are used correctly at fallible boundaries — ProviderType::parse returns Option, file I/O returns Result, and combinators (and_then, ok_or) are used idiomatically
Public API functions across the seed files are consistently typed with concrete types; no untyped generic parameters or dict-like escape hatches were observed
Feature-gated modules (recipe_config, tuple_bridge, memory_integration) use cfg-guarded inner modules with well-typed public stubs, avoiding type holes in alternate compilation paths
type_safety.issue_character: The issues are concentrated in two patterns: semantic contracts carried by String (timestamps that should be DateTime, panel IDs that should be newtypes) and structural duplication of tool-info types across crate boundaries that forces manual mapping.
type_safety.score_rationale: The codebase demonstrates disciplined Rust type use in the domain model layer — enums are not bypassed, public APIs are annotated, and the Option/Result vocabulary is used correctly. The score is held below 80 by a recurring weak-typing pattern for timestamp and identifier fields (String used where a structured type would enforce the contract), one production .expect() that breaks the error surface of GoalTree, and a parallel ToolInfo definition that forces callers to map between identical shapes. These are real maintenance liabilities but are isolated rather than systemic, placing the codebase in the high-competent range rather than excellent.

issues.summary: Timestamp fields typed as String carry ISO-8601 semantic contracts not enforced by the type
evidence: InstalledRecipe::installed_at: String (registry.rs:20) — populated by callers with RFC-3339 strings but nothing prevents arbitrary non-date strings
Goal::created_at: String, updated_at: String (goals/types.rs:53-55) — set via chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339() but stored and compared as bare strings throughout the tree
issues.suggestion: Replace String timestamp fields with chrono::DateTime<Utc>; serde's built-in support handles serialization. This makes the contract machine-verifiable and eliminates silent format mismatches.

issues.summary: GoalTree::storage_path panics instead of returning Result when home directory is missing
evidence: tree.rs:72-76: dirs::home_dir().expect("home directory must exist") inside the private storage_path helper — this is called from the public GoalTree::load which returns Result<Self>, so the error contract is broken before the ? operator can propagate it
issues.suggestion: Change storage_path to return Result<PathBuf, GoalError> and propagate the missing-home-dir case as GoalError::InvalidOperation, allowing callers to handle it rather than crashing.

issues.summary: McpToolInfo in colony-recipe and ToolInfo in colony-mcp are parallel type definitions for the same concept
evidence: McpToolInfo (mcp_lifecycle.rs:33-37): name: String, description: Option<String>, server_name: String
ToolInfo (connection.rs:56-61): tool: Tool (rmcp type embedding name/description), server_name: String
Any cross-subsystem code that needs both shapes must manually map between them, and the shapes can diverge silently
issues.suggestion: Either unify into a single canonical ToolInfo in a shared crate (colony-config or a new colony-mcp-types), or make McpToolInfo a view over ToolInfo. The divergence risks future schema drift.

issues.summary: SidebarConfig panel lists use Vec<String> where a PanelId newtype or enum would enforce validity
evidence: SidebarConfig::panels: Vec<String> and collapsed_panels: Vec<String> (manager.rs:15-16) are populated with literal panel names like "file_tree", "session", "mcp", "git_files"
The SidebarManager::on_event method matches against subscribed strings (manager.rs:158-165), creating a stringly-typed event dispatch
A typo in a panel name string silently produces a missing panel rather than a compile-time error
issues.suggestion: Define a PanelId enum with all known panel variants, or at minimum a newtype wrapper with an exhaustive from_str. This would surface panel name mismatches at compile time or at startup rather than silently.

root_causes: String used for semantic values that have narrower contracts (timestamps, identifiers, panel names) — a pattern visible across 3-4 independent subsystems, suggesting it was a deliberate early simplification that was never revisited
Parallel type definitions at crate boundaries without a shared types crate, causing ToolInfo to be re-defined independently in colony-recipe and colony-mcp
likely_symptoms: ts_panel_id_strings is likely a symptom of the broader weak-typing-for-identifiers root cause rather than an independent design decision
possible_false_positives: The #[allow(dead_code)] suppressions in tutorial sub-modules are likely intentional — the tutorial subsystem is under construction and these suppress premature cleanup warnings, not type-safety suppressions
